visual.prompt: Educational infographic: Split-scene comparison showing sound transmission through different media. LEFT SIDE: Deep underwater scene with a majestic humpback whale emitting visible concentric sound waves that travel far through crystal-clear blue water, arrows showing 'Sound travels faster' with speed label '1500 m/s', text overlay 'Communicating Whale'. RIGHT SIDE: Golden hour scene of railroad tracks extending to horizon, steam train approaching in distance, young woman with brown hair standing near tracks cupping hand to ear listening, sound wave visualization traveling through metal rails, text overlay 'Railroad Tracks' and 'Hear the train coming'. Seamless color transition from cool ocean blue to warm sunset orange. Header text: 'Sound Travels Faster in Water & Solids'. Photorealistic cinematic style, 8K resolution, educational diagram aesthetic with clean typography, dramatic lighting.
visual.textOverlay: Sound Travels Faster in Water & Solids
visual.reasoning: Immediately grabs attention with relatable scenarios (whale communication, train approach) while teaching the core physics concept. Split scene creates instant visual comparison.

kelly.pose: welcoming stance, arms slightly open, head tilted with curiosity
kelly.expression: excited wonder, eyebrows raised, bright smile

visual.prompt: Kelly teaching about sound in water. Background: underwater scene with visible sound waves, whale silhouette in distance. Kelly in foreground with diagram overlay space on right side. Soft blue lighting, educational atmosphere, professional photography, 8K.
visual.reasoning: Teaches the specific speed of sound in water with visual context.

kelly.pose: pointing gesture toward diagram area on right

optionA.imagePrompt: 512x512 educational choice card: Underwater scene with blue whale swimming, visible sound waves expanding far through crystal clear water, representing fast sound transmission. Bold text 'Through Water!' at bottom. Clean educational style, subtle green glow border indicating correct answer. High contrast, tappable mobile design.
optionA.responseScript: Exactly! Water molecules are closer together, so sound vibrations pass through much faster—about 4x faster than in air!

optionB.imagePrompt: 512x512 educational choice card: Speaker cone in air with shorter, smaller sound waves that don't travel as far. Represents slower sound in air. Bold text 'Through Air?' at bottom. Clean educational style, neutral border. High contrast, tappable mobile design.
optionB.responseScript: Sound does travel through air, but much slower! Air molecules are spread out, so it takes longer for vibrations to pass from one to the next.

visual.prompt: Kelly teaching about sound in solids. Background: cross-section of metal beam or steel rail with vibration visualization. Kelly in foreground with scientific diagram overlay. Industrial-scientific lighting, educational atmosphere, 8K.
visual.reasoning: Shows sound travels even faster in solids, completing the progression: air → water → solid.

kelly.pose: both hands gesturing to emphasize the surprising fact

optionA.imagePrompt: 512x512 educational choice card: Steel I-beam or railroad rail with intense vibration lines showing extremely fast sound transmission. Lightning-fast wave visualization. Bold text 'Through Steel!' at bottom. Clean educational style, subtle green glow border. High contrast, industrial metallic colors.
optionA.responseScript: You got it! Steel is so tightly packed that sound races through at nearly 6 kilometers per second—that's why you can hear a train through the tracks before you hear it through the air!

optionB.imagePrompt: 512x512 educational choice card: Soft foam or cotton with very weak, absorbed sound waves barely traveling. Represents sound absorption. Bold text 'Through Foam?' at bottom. Clean educational style, neutral border. Soft textures, muted colors.
optionB.responseScript: Interesting thought! Foam actually absorbs sound rather than transmitting it well—that's why we use it for soundproofing. The particles are loosely packed and don't pass vibrations efficiently.

visual.prompt: Educational infographic: Split-scene showing sound vs vacuum. LEFT: Earth atmosphere with visible sound waves traveling between people talking. RIGHT: Deep space with astronaut floating in silence, 'NO SOUND' with crossed-out speaker icon, stars in background. Dramatic contrast between vibrant Earth and empty space. 8K, educational style.
visual.reasoning: Drives home the key insight: sound NEEDS matter to travel. Space is the ultimate proof.

kelly.pose: hands spread apart showing contrast, thoughtful pose

optionA.imagePrompt: 512x512 educational choice card: Astronaut floating in starry space, surrounded by absolute silence, speaker icon with X through it, 'NO SOUND' text. Represents vacuum of space. Bold text 'Silent Space' at bottom. Clean educational style, subtle green glow border. Dark space background with stars.
optionA.responseScript: Exactly right! Space is a vacuum—there are no air molecules, no water, no solid particles to carry sound waves. That's why 'in space, no one can hear you scream'!

optionB.imagePrompt: 512x512 educational choice card: Earth seen from space with sound wave icon suggesting sound could travel anywhere. Represents common misconception. Bold text 'Sound Everywhere?' at bottom. Clean educational style, neutral border. Blue Earth against space.
optionB.responseScript: On Earth, sound is almost everywhere because we're surrounded by air, water, and solid surfaces. But step outside our atmosphere, and it's completely silent—no particles to vibrate!
